I hit the tool-call ceiling before I could package the archive. Here's where things stand — the investigation is complete, and I found something worth stopping on.

What I did
Reconstructed all 349 files from dump.txt and SHA-256 verified every one (two initially mismatched: the last file in the dump had the dump's own footer appended, and export.sh is self-referentially mangled because it prints the very separators the splitter parses — I won't ship export.sh).

Your terminal log's headline: test count is 1157, exactly as predicted. Spec is at v1.29, Slice 44 (sections-first index) is delivered — my notes said 1.28/Slice 43, so I was one slice stale.

The finding: a real defect, caught by your own run
Your first dotnet test had one failure that passed on the ci_local.sh rerun:

MenuEventLogTests.ListRecent_IsNewestFirstAcrossItemsAndRespectsTheCap
Expected: "section_changed"   Actual: "created"
That is not flakiness to retry past. Guid.CreateVersion7() is not monotonic within a millisecond. I verified against dotnet/runtime release/10.0 — it is literally NewGuid() with the 48-bit timestamp overwritten and the version/variant nibbles set. The other 74 bits stay cryptographically random, so two identifiers minted in the same millisecond sort randomly.

I modelled the byte layout and measured it:

result
same-ms pair, minted in order, compared as PostgreSQL compares	49.8% out of order
three-event create reads in minted order	16.7% (1 of 6 permutations)
with a 12-bit counter in rand_a (RFC 9562 §6.2 method 1)	0 inversions in 20k pairs, 50k across a moving clock, 10k inside one millisecond, and a backward clock step
Nine reads tie-break on a UUIDv7 identifier after occurred_at, plus OrderProjection. The sharpest instance isn't the menu at all: OrderStaging.Build mints line identifiers in a tight loop in basket order, and OrderProjection orders lines by AddedAt (identical across a batch) then OrderLineIdentifier — so a guest's basket order is scrambled on send, on their own order surface, the kitchen ticket, and the bill. On the menu it hits three surfaces including the activity feed you shipped last slice.

The property is asserted in prose in four places (MenuEventLog.cs, AdministrationMenu.razor line 248, the two test comments) and enforced nowhere — F-65's mechanism again.

And there's a trap in the fix. Guid.CompareTo compares _b — the low 16 bits of the millisecond — as a signed Int16, so it disagrees with PostgreSQL's unsigned byte-wise uuid order across a millisecond boundary. I demonstrated a concrete disagreeing pair. A Domain test asserting ordering via CompareTo would be a gate passing for the wrong reason; it has to compare ToByteArray(bigEndian: true).

Scope call I'd make for Slice 45 — tell me if you disagree
F-95 alone: the monotonic factory. Not bundled with the resequencing verb, for a stated reason: that verb writes N reordered events at one instant, so its ordering test would also be the first test of this fix, and a red run couldn't tell you which one broke. §18's "investigate any deviation from the predicted count first" is cheap with one change and expensive with two.

This is still menu progress — it repairs the Slice 40–44 surfaces and is the prerequisite for both next menu steps (the resequencing verb §7 names as an open cut, and the cross-section activity feed AdministrationMenu.razor names as absent). Slice 46 is then the resequencing verb with its Up/Down controls, which carries an F-93 obligation to add a barrier selector in the same slice.

Planned change set, all full files: UuidV7IdentifierFactory.cs, IIdentifierFactory.cs, UuidV7IdentifierFactoryTests.cs (2 → 7 facts, so predicted count 1162), TestingSectionContractTests.cs (MinimumCountedClasses 19 → 20), MenuEventLog.cs (comment only), plus spec → v1.30 (§8.1, §16.4, Appendix A F-95, changelog), ADR-0011, DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, BUILD_PROGRESS.md, MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, _CHANGES.md. No migration, no deletions.

Two things I'll record under "what was NOT verified": there's no .NET SDK in this container and dotnet.microsoft.com isn't reachable, so the C# is not compiled — the ordering proof is the Python model above, not a test run. I will not touch AdministrationMenu.razor (its line-248 comment becomes true rather than aspirational, so it needs no edit) — your menuSectionSummary fix stays exactly as you made it.

Say "continue" and I'll build the archive.

Root cause against dotnet/runtime release/10.0 — CreateVersion7 is NewGuid() + timestamp overwrite. No counter, no monotonic state.
Byte-accurate model: 49.8% of same-ms pairs inverted before, 0/20,000 after; three-event create read correctly 16.7% before; 0 inversions across a moving clock, counter overflow (timestamp borrows 2ms), and a backward clock step.
The shipped Create's exact byte arithmetic, transliterated and run — 5,000 in one ms: 0 inversions, all version 7, all variant 0x80, sort keys distinct.

The original failure was 50%, so one green run isn't evidence. Please run it a few times:

Create_MintsDistinctSortKeysUnderConcurrency uses Parallel.For, and a CAS loop's first real test is its first real run.

The guest-basket consequence has no test in this slice — OrderProjection is now correct but nothing asserts a multi-line send reads back in basket order. It's named in Still open, not quietly closed.

Veto points
The resequencing verb is deliberately not here, though you asked for menu progress. A resequence writes several reordered events in one transaction at one instant — which is this slice's property — so its ordering test would have been the first test of this fix, and a red run couldn't say which change caused it. Stage 3a carries the full design (interface shape, the whole-list-not-pairwise ruling, lock ordering, the no-op rule, the F-93 selector obligation) so Slice 46 is arrangement, not design. If you'd rather have had both in one archive, say so and I'll fold them together.

_lastSortKey is static. To make it per-instance: drop static from the field and NextSortKey, and delete Create_AscendsAcrossTwoInstances.

Four comments were repointed rather than deleted, departing from F-77. Reasoning in _CHANGES.md: F-77 governs a count nothing can check; this was a claim right about the mechanism and wrong about its source, so it now names a contract a test can fail.
